Test Case Test
Case
test if the requirements of a function are respected and if
everything corresponds to what is required in the specifications.
To be able to cover in a total way a requirement, for each test
case must be contemplated as a 'positive test' that a 'negative
test', that is, for each operating condition must be provided for
the case in which the test covers a certain requirement and at
the same time a test should be provided in which, if the opposite
case is applied, this must give an opposite result to the previous
case.
Only in this way are all possible cases covered and the test is
robust.

format - 1 - Test Case

format -1-Test Case
A test is formalized in a document that describes in detail how it should be done. Each test can be set up
like this:
o A unique identifier such as an alphanumeric number or string
o The name of the function to which it belongs
o The name of the project for which it is written
o The market to which it is addressed, for example if it is a market in Europe rather than Asia or America
o The type of test, for example if it is an integration or diagnostic test
o The preconditions, fundamental for the success of the test
o Actions, which describe what must be done starting from the preconditions described above
o The check to be carried out after the actions, ie the expected result of the test
o The result of the test, which can be OK or KO
o The name of the functional specification from which the test is extracted
o Any notes to complete the test in case the tester needs to add comments

slides.body:
the functional requirement to the test case -1-From
To get to the writing of a test case we start from the functional requirements, described in the
specification or VF.
It starts from the analysis of the specification which is one of the most important steps useful for the
clean writing of the tests:
for VF analysis, we mean the study process of a vehicle function and any changes to be made to the
test, following an accurate comparison between the requirements themselves, DB Files, already
performed test results, related documentation.
The changes can be of various kinds, from the wrong nomenclature of a signal with respect to the DB
File where it is contained (or even to its absence), parts of function developed on exchange of internal
messages that can not be tested with a view to integration testing.
Before you can get to write the test there is a procedure to be followed so that the test cases are
correct and functional, shown below.

slides.title: the functional requirement to the test case - 3 - From One must assume that the tests have to 'cover' a totally specific
slides.body:
the functional requirement to the test case -3-From
One must assume that the tests have to 'cover' a totally specific, that is, you
must write all tests useful to test all that is written in a VF and predict, as we
said before, even against all cases.
It can happen that downstream of the analysis of the requirements you realize
that there may be additional test cases and that, if plausible, must still be
written, even if not explicitly present in VF.
There are also cases in which there are requirements in VF, with which are
described the 'internal' behavior to the component that can not be monitored.
That type of test, identified as a 'component test', is the responsibility of the
supplier of the component itself who is concerned with carrying out its tests.

slides.title: procedure - 1 - Test When all the tests for a VF are written, proceed with the actual tests. The test phase can be perfo
slides.body:
procedure -1-Test
The test phase can be performed in several ways:
1. In the car
2. At the bench
3. At the simulator
This depends on the type of test to be performed.

slides.title: procedure - 2 - Test 1. It is preferred to do a test in the car when it is necessary to see, on the user's side, the rea
slides.body:
procedure -2-Test
the real behavior of a given action. For example, if you want to test the behavior of
the windscreen wipers at a high vehicle speed, so as to verify the user's real
behavior in a given condition.
2. We proceed with the bench tests when it is necessary to simulate / measure the
electric / electronic behavior, for example when you have to carry out tests
involving currents and / or voltages, also by means of an oscilloscope
3. We test the simulator when you do not have a car or a bench, or when you need
the simulation of CAN messages, whose dynamics are very fast.
